name: THE BOUNTIFUL NUGGET
note: Doc 05 Room 3 plus doc 16, verbatim. Twelve hotspots and two exits. THE HANDBILL is the Rules of the Assay and carries Rule 3. THE PATRONS has no drawn figures in the background -- doc 07's ambient characters supply them at runtime, so the rect covers where they stand. Doc 16 note 4: the stove's third LISTEN reverses the first two on purpose; it has gone out and nobody has noticed. Do not 'correct' it.

LOOK_AT.say: A hand of cards, face up, abandoned. A very good hand.
repeat: Still there. Nobody's claimed it. Nobody's cleared it. Nobody's even looked at it, except me, a lot.
I have decided he is coming back. I have decided this several times, each time more firmly.
then: Somebody walked away from it and went outside. I'd have stayed for a much worse one.

LISTEN_TO.say: Quiet. Cards don't say much when nobody's holding them.
repeat: Not a whisper.
Nothing. Whoever he was, he isn't in the building.

overrides.PICK_UP: It isn't my hand. If it were, I'd be a lot more cheerful.
overrides.USE: I don't play. My father was very clear about that, and he was wrong about most things, so I've been meaning to start.

LISTEN_TO.say: Paper. It's been on this wall so long it's stopped being read.
repeat: Paper, lifting a little in the draft from the door. Still unread.
Silence. It has outlasted everyone who nailed it up.

LOOK_AT.say: RULES OF THE ASSAY. One: a man may not be interrupted in his account. Two: a man's account may be doubted only by a better one. Three: truth is admissible but has never been raised. Four: the judges' decision is final and may be appealed to the same judges. Five: no firearms, no knives, no arithmetic.
repeat: Rule five forbids arithmetic. There's a story behind that, and I'd pay good money to hear it, if I could count it out.
Rule four: you may appeal the judges' decision to the same judges. Somebody thought that through, and nailed it up anyway.

overrides.PICK_UP: It's nailed on. Thoroughly. Somebody wanted the rules to stay up a great deal more than they wanted them read.

LOOK_AT.say: A spittoon, placed optimistically far from anyone sitting down.
repeat: The floor around it tells the story of a town that has tried, and tried, and missed.
Brass. Somebody polished this once. I'd like to know what they'd done to deserve it.
Yes. Again. There's a man at the bar with tremendous range and no aim.
I've stopped listening to the spittoon. Best decision I've made in the territory.

LOOK_AT.say: A portrait of a man in a good collar, hung crooked. Nobody in here knows who he is.
repeat: A governor, a founder, and 'that's Bill's uncle.' Bill was not available to confirm.
It's the same photograph the Clarion prints as Obadiah Mott. I'm almost sure. I'm keeping that to myself until I'm sure.
then: I asked three people and got three answers.

LISTEN_TO.say: Silent. He's kept quiet about who he is for years.
repeat: Not a word. Not even a crooked one.
Nothing. He's a man in Ohio, and nobody here is asking him.

LOOK_AT.say: The stove, still lit. I've been buried since I last looked at it, and it's still the warmest thing in here.
A cast-iron stove, lit, in July. Nobody's said anything. I'm not going to be the first.
repeat: Still lit. The man beside it hasn't taken his coat off since I arrived in the territory. I'm beginning to think he can't.
The warmest thing in Consolation, wasted on a room full of men who've already warmed themselves the other way.

LISTEN_TO.say: It ticks. The one thing in this room doing honest work.
repeat: Tick. Tick. Still working. Still the only one.
Nothing. It's gone out, and nobody has noticed.

overrides.OPEN: It's lit. I'm not opening a lit stove in a wooden building full of drunk men. I've read how that story ends. Everyone has.
overrides.PULL: Every man in the room is suddenly watching. The pipe stays. My reputation very nearly didn't.

LOOK_AT.say: I tune it Thursdays now. It's the only thing in Consolation that comes out more honest after I've been at it.
Tuned, and staying tuned. The room plays it softer now, like it knows what it cost.
An upright, hauled four hundred miles by mule at ten times what it's worth.
repeat: Nobody's touched it since I came in. I check. I check more than is healthy.
Bottle rings on the lid. Several. They are using a piano as a table, and I am being very calm about it.
then: Nobody here can play it. I could make it worth playing. I'd only need asking.

LISTEN_TO.say: A. Four hundred and forty. In this town, at last, that's not a foreign language.
C-sharp is a semitone flat, and has been for years. Nobody's noticed.
repeat: C-sharp. Still flat. It's like a stone in my shoe, if my shoe were across the room.
I could put it right in four minutes. I've started thinking about it at mealtimes.
then: I've noticed. I've noticed several times.

overrides.USE: I could tune it. Nobody's asked. I'm not going to ask to be asked. I'm going to stand near it until somebody has the idea.
overrides.OPEN: The lid comes up. Inside: a piano. Exactly what I expected, and somehow still a letdown.
overrides.PUSH: I lean on it. It doesn't budge. It hasn't moved since it arrived, and the floor has grown round it like a tree round a nail.
overrides.TALK_TO: Soon. We'll talk properly soon. Not in front of everyone.

LOOK_AT.say: A window onto Main Street. The cleanest thing in the building, because it's the only thing in here anybody looks at.
repeat: From in here the street looks almost respectable. That's what windows are for.
Somebody's scratched a name into the pane. Not one I know. I checked it for mine anyway, out of habit.

LISTEN_TO.say: The street, muffled. Two men arguing about a boundary.
repeat: The boundary again. Neither of them has given an inch.
The stage is in. Four days from Sacramento, and eleven new men who think they're early.

LOOK_AT.say: A chandelier. Underneath it, a dirt floor. The two have never been introduced.
repeat: Brass, crystal, and a dirt floor. Somebody made a decision about priorities. I'd like to shake his hand, and then check my pockets.
They light it after I've gone, apparently. It's always cooling when I come in.
Ticking, cooling, hanging over mud.
Nothing. All that money, and it has nothing to say for itself.
then: The most expensive object in the territory, and it's hanging over mud.

overrides.PULL: It's nine feet up and heavier than I am. I'll admire it from down here, like everyone else.

LOOK_AT.say: Stairs, up to rooms I haven't been invited to. There's a man on the landing.
repeat: He hasn't moved. I'm starting to think he isn't waiting for anything. He came with the stairs.
Eleven steps. I've counted them from down here, which is as far up as I've got.
then: There is always a man on the landing.

LISTEN_TO.say: Boards, overhead. Somebody pacing a room about the size of mine.
repeat: Four steps, turn. Four steps, turn. Definitely the size of mine.
He's stopped. Somehow that's worse.

overrides.USE: I haven't been invited up, and I'm not going to invite myself. I have been practicing looking like someone who might be.

LOOK_AT.say: Nine men drinking to Mott's strike, up at seven to dig for it. I could tell them. I'm not sure who that would help.
Nine men drinking after dark. Every one of them was at his claim by seven this morning, and will be again by seven tomorrow. This is the bit in between.
repeat: The same nine. I can tell them apart now. I don't think that's good news for me.
They're talking about where the gold is. They've been talking about where the gold is for twelve years. Nobody has gone and got it.

LISTEN_TO.say: Talk, all at the same volume. I came up once, between a mule and the price of flour.
Talk. Lots of it, all at the same volume, none of it listened to.
repeat: A man in the corner has told the same story four times. It's grown twice. There's a bear in it now.
The word 'Mott' comes up about once a minute. I've timed it. It's once a minute.

overrides.TALK_TO: I've tried. They're very friendly. They want to know what I know. I know nothing, and it disappoints them fresh every time.

LOOK_AT.say: I look like a man who has recently been buried and is being brave about it.
I look like a man who knows something the whole room doesn't. It's not a good look on me. I'm keeping it.
I look like a man who has recently been robbed and is being brave about it.
repeat: Still me. I'd hoped for some improvement. The coat is doing its best.
Give it a few weeks and I'll look like I belong here. That was never the plan.

LISTEN_TO.say: Quiet. Mirrors never say anything. It's the only restraint they show.
repeat: Still quiet. I keep expecting it to say something about the coat.
Nothing. I keep checking. It keeps not.

LOOK_AT.say: They drank to my memory on Tuesday. I was there. I'm told I was spoken of very warmly, briefly, between rounds.
Mahogany. Genuine mahogany.
repeat: Mahogany, four hundred miles from the nearest tree that could have grown it. I'd like to meet the mule.
The best-kept surface in town, and it's a bar. I don't think that's an accident.
then: Somebody spent real money on the one surface everybody leans on.

LISTEN_TO.say: My name — one of its spellings — in a toast. It's a strange vintage, being remembered at cost price.

repeat: Glasses. Talk. The bear is now eleven feet tall and has a grievance.
Somebody's being served ahead of somebody else, and it's being noticed.
then: The story in the corner is on its fifth telling, and the bear has a name now.

overrides.PUSH: It doesn't move. It's the only thing in town built to stay.
overrides.OPEN: The barman watches me consider it. We both put the idea down gently.

LOOK_AT.say: Batwing doors, from the inside. They swing both ways. From in here, that reads as a warning.
repeat: The street, past them. Somehow it's a surprise every time.
Six inches of boardwalk and then the mud. I know exactly how far now. My boots know it better.

LISTEN_TO.say: The street. It sounds busier from in here than it is.
repeat: Boots on the boardwalk. Somebody deciding whether to come in. Deciding no.
Nothing. Everyone who's coming in is in.

LOOK_AT.say: A door behind the bar, shut. There's a room back there where things get settled.
repeat: Shut. It's been shut every time I've looked. That isn't the same as locked, and I've thought about the difference a lot.
Shut in a way that's been decided, not just closed. I didn't know doors could do that. This one can.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Whatever happens back there happens quietly, and then everyone agrees about it.
repeat: A pencil. Somebody is writing something down.
Two men going in. A while later, two men coming out, and one of them pleased.

overrides.PUSH: It gives half an inch and stops. There's a chair against it. I apologize to the chair.

entrances.note: Through the batwing doors on the left wall, facing right into the room.

Back out of the back room, on the floor in front of the bar's near end (floor_1), LEFT of where Deke Vessel stands (at 1035,815 since 2026-11-01 his figure spans x 937-1133, nearer the camera): at 930 Thad arrived half behind him, and at the door's own x wholly. retiredNote:
THE 320x144 RELICS ARE GONE. This room carried an `idles` layer declaring four 18-pixel figures against a sheet drawn for the retired 320x144 presentation, and a foreground plane of the same vintage -- both drawn into a 1920x864 room, which is what put black boxes on the floor and one beside Thad. They described the same men who are now baked into the plates: the bar’s near and middle drinkers, a seated player, and doc 16’s man beside the stove.
THE MAN ON THE LANDING SURVIVES THE DELETION, because he was never in that list. Ruling 20 makes him an explicit exception -- his whole joke is that he never moves -- and doc 16 keeps him in THE STAIRS: there is always a man on the landing.

accost.note: Doc 35, VESSEL'S AUTO-OPEN, exactly: on entering, unless the swindle has happened or he has already opened, wait 1500 ms, he says "You're the piano man." (his tree's opening, extracted from doc 27's Root) and the tree opens; T_VESSEL_OPENED makes it once only. Thad does not walk to him (doc 27: 'He opens. Thad does not approach him.').

figureLight.note: Tyler, 2026-11-01: Thad and Deke 'look different from the rest of the characters in the room... the other characters all seem to have more detail and are a little darker.' The bar men and card players were drawn for this room and carry its lamplight; Thad is drawn in even, neutral light so he can go in every room, and Deke's shadows are shallower than his neighbours'. Measured on the sprites against the six patrons (mean luminance 47, darkest tenth 12): Thad 58/17, Deke 53/26. This grade (variant B of three shown to Tyler) lights both with a warm multiply [1, 0.9, 0.78] -- gentle enough to keep Thad's coat blue -- taking Thad to about 47/14; Deke also gets more contrast, because his darks never reached the room's, landing at about 33/8. Tyler, 2026-11-01: "B but Deke ever so slightly brighter" -- his brightness 0.85 to 0.9.

Generated once (art/staging/room-03/barrel-01, room-03-barrel 1 of 2), keyed and BOX-reduced by tools/art/cut-prop.py to 225 px to the rim -- 0.53 of Deke's 428, his belt -- and graded to the bar front by tools/grade/match-neighbours.py at 0.9. Spans x 817-962, clear of Deke's rest-pose left edge at about 981. Then darkened by tools/art/darken-prop.py, now at brightness 0.75 with the base falling to 0.7 (Tyler, 2026-11-01: "It's too bright. Please darken it so it fits in better." Chosen from 0.8, 0.7 and 0.6 rendered in the room; 0.6 went muddy). Then 0.75 (Tyler, 2026-11-01: "Maybe ever so slightly lighter since the floor behind it is so bright?").
